rv.q: Zak’s production of MR. PARKER showcases the impressive talents of seasoned actors and a promising Chicago debut.
Michael McKeever’s play has something important and meaningful to say to each of us.
His words are embraced, fully, through director David Zak's nuanced shaping of the show's fine cast.
Overall, I recommend MR PARKER as an excellent theatrical experience.
Anchored by Andrew Kain Miller's performance in the title role, this is a quiet show about big feelings that settles in comfortably in the basement black-box space.
This production of Mr. Parker is electric.
Mr. Parker doesn’t feel like a stereotypical grief journey written for a show with a linear progression of healing.
